extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political economy; policymakers and historians of public finance
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic exposition of different kinds of taxes (poll, stamp, succession, capitation, consumption, wages) and their economic incidence — who ultimately pays and how taxes affect capital, labour, prices, and public revenue. Draws on historical examples (England, France, Holland, Bohemia, Rome) to illustrate principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poll-taxes on bondmen vs poll-taxes on freemen
rubrics_metrics.description: Poll-taxes of so much a head upon the bondmen employed in cultivation seem anciently to have been common all over Europe. Poll-taxes have often been represented as badges of slavery. A poll tax upon slaves is altogether different from a poll-tax upon freemen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the two types: a poll tax on freemen is paid by the persons upon whom it is imposed and is often arbitrary or unequal; a poll on slaves is paid by owners (masters) and, though unequal in some respects, is not arbitrary because masters know exactly how many slaves they have to pay for. Historical framing informs incidence judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes upon men- and maid-servants as taxes on expense
rubrics_metrics.description: The taxes which in Holland are imposed upon men and maid servants are taxes, not upon stock, but upon expense; and so far resemble the taxes upon consumable commodities. The tax of a guinea a-head for every man-servant... falls heaviest upon the middling rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat per-head servant taxes as consumption/expense taxes: they disproportionately burden the middling classes (can affect demand for servants), leave the poor unaffected, and are distinct from property taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes upon the profits of stock and their effect on interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes upon the profits of stock, in particular employments, can never affect the interest of money. Taxes upon the revenue arising from stock in all employments, where the government attempts to levy them with any degree of exactness, will, in many cases, fall upon the interest of money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a tax is precisely levied on revenue from stock; if exact, it may reduce the interest (or be capitalised into prices/rates). Use examples like the French vingtième to analyze incidence on annuities and capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes upon transference of property diminish capital value
rubrics_metrics.description: When property changes hands ... such taxes have frequently been imposed upon it as necessarily take away some part of its capital value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any duty on inheritance, sale, transfer, or registration that reduces the capital value should be seen as diminishing funds available for productive labour. Consider whether tax is direct or indirect and whether it applies on transference frequency—this affects equality and thrift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamp duties and registration as indirect taxes on movable property
rubrics_metrics.description: The transference of stock or moveable property ... has been taxed indirectly ... by requiring that the deed ... should be written upon paper or parchment which had paid a certain stamp duty ... secondly, by requiring ... that it should be recorded ... and by imposing certain duties upon such registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stamp and registration requirements as instruments to tax otherwise concealably transferred assets. Assess proportionality, ease of enforcement, and arbitrary effects (e.g., confiscation for undervalued stamps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession and inheritance duties (vicesima hereditatum / Dutch system)
rubrics_metrics.description: The vicesima hereditatum ... was a tax upon the transference of property from the dead to the living. In Holland collateral successions are taxed according to the degree of relation, from five to thirty per cent. ... Direct successions ... pay no tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating inheritance taxes consider relationship-based scales, exemptions for nearest relations, and political/social rationale (mitigating cruelty to dependents). Historical examples show varied progressivity and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feudal transference incidents (relief, minority rentes, fines on alienation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The heir of every immediate vassal of the crown paid a certain duty, generally a year’s rent, upon receiving the investiture ... If the heir was a minor, the whole rents ... devolved to the superior ... By a feudal law, the vassal could not alienate without the consent of his superior, who generally extorted a fine or composition on granting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legacy feudal charges as taxes on transfers that often operated as significant sovereign revenue. Note effects on estate management (long minorities could produce waste) and how fines became proportioned to sale price in some countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes on sale of land and houses — incidence on seller vs buyer
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes upon the sale of land fall altogether upon the seller. ... Taxes upon the sale of new-built houses, where the building is sold without the ground, fall generally upon the buyer ... Taxes upon the sale of old houses ... fall generally upon the seller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide incidence by considering necessity and bargaining power: sellers often forced to sell bear tax; builders of new houses can pass tax to buyers if profit margins require it. Market conditions (demand, bankruptcies) change incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of mortgages and deeds: public benefit vs abuses of secret registers
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration of mortgages ... as it gives great security both to creditors and purchasers, is extremely advantageous to the public. That of the greater part of deeds of other kinds, is frequently inconvenient and even dangerous ... All registers which ought to be kept secret, ought certainly never to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote registration that increases security and public good; oppose secret or proliferated registers used to extract fees (a revenue source), which create extortion and reliance on officers' probity. Evaluate which documents truly merit registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamp duties on consumables and licences as consumption taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Such stamp duties as those in England upon cards and dice, upon newspapers ... are properly taxes upon consumption; the final payment falls upon the persons who use or consume such commodities. Such stamp duties as those upon licences to retail ale, wine, and spiritous liquors ... are likewise finally paid by the consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify stamp duties according to whether they are consumption taxes (final burden on consumers) or duties on transactions; analyze pass-through to consumers and distributional impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wages of labour regulated by demand for labour and price of provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The wages of the inferior classes of work men ... are everywhere necessarily regulated by two different circumstances; the demand for labour, and the ordinary or average price of provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing tax effects on wages, always account for labour demand conditions and staple prices. These two determinants set the baseline real wage that policy can alter only indirectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct tax on wages raises nominal wages by more than the tax proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct tax upon the wages of labour ... If a tax of one-fifth ... was imposed upon wages ... after paying the tax, he should have ten shillings a-week free wages. But ... the price of labour must ... rise ... to twelve and sixpence; that is, in order to enable him to pay a tax of one-fifth, his wages must necessarily soon rise, not one-fifth part only, but one-fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use algebraic incidence reasoning: a wage tax tends to raise money wages more than the nominal tax proportion because employers advance the tax via higher gross wages, so final incidence often falls on employers/consumers/landlords depending on sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-run incidence of wage taxes falls on landlords and consumers indirectly
rubrics_metrics.description: The rise which such a tax might occasion in the wages of manufacturing labour would be advanced by the master manufacturer ... the final payment ... will fall upon the consumer. The rise ... in the wages of country labour would be advanced by the farmer ... the final payment of this rise of wages ... would, in this case, fall upon the landlord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace the chain of advances: manufacturers/masters or farmers initially pay higher wages but recover via higher prices or retained produce — ultimate burden shifts to consumers and landlords depending on industry and rural/urban context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct taxes on wages can reduce demand for labour and shrink production
rubrics_metrics.description: If direct taxes upon the wages of labour have not always occasioned a proportionable rise in those wages, it is because they have generally occasioned a considerable fall in the demand of labour. The declension of industry ... have generally been the effects of such taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for general-equilibrium effects: heavy wage taxes may reduce employment, industry size, and overall annual produce, so incidence analysis must include potential negative demand responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes upon emoluments of public offices are more politically acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The emoluments of offices ... are, perhaps, in most countries, higher than it requires ... The emoluments of offices, therefore, can, in most cases, very well bear to be taxed. ... a tax upon their emoluments ... is always a very popular tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider political economy: taxing office emoluments may be administratively easy and publicly popular; exemptions (pensions, military pay) may be politically negotiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitation (poll) taxes: arbitrary if proportioned to fortune; unequal if by rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitation taxes, if it is attempted to proportion them to the fortune or revenue of each contributor, become altogether arbitrary. Capitation taxes, if they are proportioned, not to the supposed fortune, but to the rank of each contributor, become altogether unequal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers must choose between certainty (rank-based tariffs) and equality (fortune-based assessment) — each has trade-offs: fortune-based assessment requires intrusive, arbitrary inquiries; rank-based is simpler but unequal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of capitation taxes: England vs France examples
rubrics_metrics.description: In the different poll-taxes ... the contributors were ... assessed according to the degree of their rank. In the capitation which has been levied in France ... the highest orders of people are rated according to their rank ... the lower orders ... according to what is supposed to be their fortune, by an assessment which varies from year to year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate capitation regimes by enforcement style and centralization: mild governments may accept undercollection; more severe systems fix quotas for local officials leading to over-assessment or extraction. Consider implications for taxpayer burden and state revenue reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumable commodities taxes hinge on classification: necessaries vs luxuries
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumable commodities are either necessaries or luxuries. By necessaries I understand ... whatever the custom of the country renders it indecent for creditable people, even of the lowest order, to be without. All other things I call luxuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing commodity taxes, classify goods by social custom as necessaries or luxuries, not purely by biological necessity. This classification materially affects distributional consequences and wage adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax on necessaries operates like a direct tax on wages and raises wages
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax upon those articles [necessaries] necessarily raises their price somewhat higher than the amount of the tax ... Such a tax must, therefore, occasion a rise in the wages of labour, proportionable to this rise of price. It is thus that a tax upon the necessaries of life operates exactly in the same manner as a direct tax upon the wages of labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect taxes on necessities to increase nominal wages (to preserve real subsistence), with employers or producers advancing costs and final consumers bearing the burden. Analyze pass-through and feedback into prices of other goods.
